posts: 💡 Small business tip: claim and complete your Google Business Profile. Add your opening hours, phone number, photos and services so people searching nearby can find and contact you.
📱 Most people browse on their phones. If your website is hard to read or use on a small screen, visitors may leave. Check yours on your own phone today.
🌍 Small business tip: a .co.za domain tells South African customers you're local, and it's easy to remember. Keep your domain name short and simple to spell.
✉️ Looking professional matters. An email address like info@yourbusiness.co.za builds more trust than a free webmail address on your quotes and invoices.
📅 Make it easy to buy from you. Online booking lets customers book at any hour, even when you're closed or busy with another client.
⭐ Ask happy customers for a review. Reviews help new customers trust you, so a short, friendly request after a job is well done goes a long way.
🔍 SEO basics: use clear page titles, describe your services in plain words, and mention your town or area so local customers can find you.
🔒 Check for the padlock. An SSL certificate (the padlock next to your web address) keeps data private between your visitor and your site, and customers look for it.
📞 Put your phone number and a clear call-to-action at the top of your website. Don't make customers hunt for how to contact you.
🖼️ Use real photos of your work, team and products. Genuine images build more trust than generic ones, and they make your business feel real.
⚡ Slow websites lose visitors. Compress large images and keep pages simple so your site loads quickly, especially on mobile data.
💬 Reply quickly. Customers who message your business often contact several others too, so a fast, friendly reply can win the job.
💾 Back up your website regularly. If something breaks or is hacked, a recent backup means you can get back online quickly.
🧭 Keep your details consistent. Use the same business name, address and phone number on your website, Google Business Profile and social media.
🗓️ Keep a simple posting routine. Posting a little and often on your business Page works better than a burst of posts followed by weeks of silence.
📸 Photograph your work as you go. Before-and-after shots, finished jobs and happy customers (with their permission) make great content later.
🏷️ Be clear about what you sell. Visitors should understand what your business does within a few seconds of landing on your homepage.
🧾 Put your prices or a starting price on your website where you can. It saves time and attracts people who are ready to buy.
📍 Add your service area to your website and Google Business Profile so local customers know you cover their suburb or town.
🔗 Link your website, Facebook Page and Instagram to each other so customers can find you wherever they look first.
🕒 Keep your business hours up to date online, including public holidays. Customers get frustrated by a closed door they didn't expect.
📝 Write your website text for customers, not for yourself. Explain the problem you solve and what happens when they contact you.
📲 Make your phone number tappable on mobile so customers can call you with one touch.
🎯 One clear next step per page works best: Call us, Book now or Get a quote. Too many choices can confuse visitors.
💌 Collect email addresses from customers who agree to hear from you. A simple newsletter keeps you in touch without paying for ads.
🧠 Answer common questions on your website (an FAQ section). It saves you repeating yourself and helps people decide to buy.
🔐 Use strong, different passwords for your website, email and social accounts, and switch on two-step verification where you can.
🔄 Keep your website software and plugins updated. Out-of-date software is a common way sites get hacked.
🖥️ Test your website on different devices and browsers. What looks good on your laptop might look different on a customer's phone.
🏁 Make the booking or contact form short. The fewer fields you ask people to fill in, the more likely they are to finish it.
💳 Offer simple, trusted payment options if you sell online. Customers abandon checkouts when they don't recognise the payment method.
🛍️ Good product photos sell. Use plenty of light, a clean background and a few angles for every product in your online store.
📦 Be upfront about delivery times and costs in your online store. Surprises at checkout are a top reason people leave.
🔎 Describe each product in your own words with sizes, materials and uses. It helps customers and helps search engines too.
🤝 Reply to reviews, good and bad, politely. It shows future customers that you care about service.
👥 Ask a friendly customer to share your Page with their friends. Word of mouth is still powerful, and online it travels further.
🧩 Use the same logo, colours and tone everywhere. Consistency helps people recognise and remember your business.
🗂️ Keep your customer details organised in one place, such as a simple spreadsheet or CRM, so no enquiry gets lost.
⏰ Follow up on enquiries within a day. Many customers go with the first business that gets back to them.
📈 Check which of your posts get the most likes and comments, and make more of that kind of content.
🎥 Short videos showing your work or answering a customer question can feel more personal than a text-only post.
🧼 Keep your website clean and uncluttered. White space makes content easier to read, especially on small screens.
📣 Tell people what to do at the end of a post: call, message, book or visit your website. A clear call to action gets more response.
🏪 Even if you're a one-person business, a website makes you look established and gives customers a place to check you out.
🔤 Pick a business name that is easy to spell and say, and make sure your domain and social handles match it where possible.
🌙 An online store or booking page is open when you're asleep. Customers can order or book whenever suits them.
🧑‍💼 Use a professional profile picture and cover image on your Facebook Page so it looks trustworthy at first glance.
🔔 Turn on notifications for your Page messages so you can reply to customers quickly.
📊 Look at your website visitor numbers now and then. Knowing where visitors come from helps you decide where to spend your time.
🖋️ Proofread before posting. Spelling mistakes in a flyer, post or website can make a business look careless.
🪪 Show your business registration, address or contact details on your website. It reassures customers that you're real.
🧭 Make it easy to navigate. Keep your menu short and use plain words like Services, About and Contact.
🏆 Show your best work first. Put your strongest photos or project examples near the top of your gallery or portfolio page.
